newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end down on profit taking, weather.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end down on profit taking, weather.

text.p: Continued good growing weather for South American oilseed crops spurred a wave of late selling from independent traders that pressured soybean futures at the close Tuesday, floor sources said.

Forecasters continued to indicate periodic beneficial rains for crops in Brazil throughout the week. Those conditions were said to be boosting the size of the crop and in turn, weighed on futures, traders said.
Some of the late weakness in soybeans was also tied to profit taking on long positions following Monday's sharp advances, traders said.
Support in the market stemmed from ideas that world demand for soybeans would remain good into the new year in a time when most world oilseed crops were smaller, sources said.
"The story is in the beans," a floor trader said. "It is going to take awhile, but we're going to see higher prices."
Buying by soybean crushers also helped stave off sharper losses, floor traders said.
Soybeans settled down 6-3/4 cents per bushel to down 4-1/2 cent, with January down 5 cents per bushel at $7.06-1/2, and Mar closed down 5-1/2 cents per bushel at 7.01-1/2 cents.
On the day, Refco bought 2.5 million bushels January and sold 2 million bushels March. LIT sold 500,000 bushels Jan and sold 1.2 million Mar.
Soybean volume was estimated at 40,000 contracts. That figure compared with the 44,825 traded on Monday, according to the CBOT.
In soybean options trading, Continental Grain sold 250 Mar $7.00 puts, Farmers Commodities Corp sold 100 Mar $7.00 calls, and Cargill Investor Services sold 200 Mar $7.25 puts.
Soybean options volume was estimated at 12,000 contracts, versus the 11,740 traded on Monday.
